notes.summary: Partial P15.2 theorem for a supplied surjective holomorphic fibration of smooth compact Kähler manifolds with theta=pi*beta: the calibrated base BT operator is independent of auxiliary Kähler class and bounded uniformly converging perturbative potentials, without descent or an epsilon-relative rate, including singular fibres. The original general atom remains open.
notes.detailedSummary: For n>nu>=1, m=n-nu, beta Kähler on B, every Kähler omega on X gives pi_*(omega^m)=c_omega>0 globally, with generic-fibre and cohomological meanings. For bounded beta-psh phi and any bounded (theta+epsilon omega)-psh u_epsilon converging uniformly to phi composed with pi, the pushed-forward top BT measures divided by binom(n,nu)c_omega epsilon^m converge weakly to (beta+ddc phi)^nu, with raw mass int_B beta^nu. The scaled difference estimate is O(||u_epsilon-pi*phi||_infinity), requiring no epsilon-relative rate. Local decreasing BT approximation proves projection through critical fibres; positive remainders have mass O(epsilon). The corresponding scaled bounded energy converges to the base Aubin–Mabuchi energy and satisfies the bounded cocycle, segment variational, monotonicity, concavity and shift laws. The results allow arbitrary fixed auxiliary Kähler classes and smoothly convergent auxiliary forms with Kähler limit, after their respective calibrations. Compensated changes of beta representative preserve the operator and change energy by the reference cocycle. No canonical carrier construction for general pseudoeffective classes, minimum-reference theorem, unbounded P-type/E1 extension, or degenerate auxiliary path is established. This is an author proof draft, not an independent verification or priority claim.
notes.text:
Partial P15.2 result: a relative base operator for the supplied-fibration bounded scope. This is an unverified author proof draft, not a claim of independent verification or literature priority. The original general pseudoeffective zero-volume P15.2 remains open.

Statement and reference data. Let pi:X->B be supplied, surjective and holomorphic between connected smooth compact Kähler manifolds, dim_C X=n>nu=dim_C B>=1; set m=n-nu. No connected-fibre, smooth-fibre, equidimensionality or flatness hypothesis is imposed. Supply a Kähler form beta on B and put theta=pi*beta. Use ddc=i/(2pi)partial barpartial and dc=i/(4pi)(barpartial-partial). Every potential is its upper semicontinuous psh representative, and every norm is the pointwise supremum norm. Products are ordinary bounded Bedford–Taylor products.

For every Kähler form omega on X, pi_*(omega^m)=c_omega is a positive constant on all of B. Put K_omega=binom(n,nu)c_omega and V_B=int_B beta^nu. For every globally bounded beta-psh phi, set U=phi composed with pi and C=beta+ddc phi. For ANY globally bounded (theta+epsilon omega)-psh u_epsilon with delta_epsilon=||u_epsilon-U||_infinity->0, the measures

pi_*((theta+epsilon omega+ddc u_epsilon)^n)/(K_omega epsilon^m)

converge weakly on B against every continuous test to C^nu. The raw mass is V_B>0. The u_epsilon need not descend, and no epsilon-relative rate is required. The exact family U is always admissible. The carrier B has dimension nu; the reference potential is 0, current beta, and raw mass V_B. The operator retains bounded/minimal singularity type and the actual potential modulo constants, not only a singularity-equivalence class. The supplied fibration/carrier and base reference class are additional data; their minimality or canonical extraction from alpha is not established.

The associated unnormalized Aubin–Mabuchi energies satisfy

E_{theta+epsilon omega}(u_epsilon)/(K_omega epsilon^m) -> E_beta(phi),
E_gamma(v)=1/(d+1) sum_{j=0}^d int_Y v(gamma+ddc v)^j gamma^{d-j},

where Y is compact of complex dimension d and gamma is Kähler. Both limits are independent of every fixed auxiliary Kähler representative AND class, using its own c_omega. The constant c_omega itself can depend on the class. The limits also hold for omega_epsilon converging smoothly on X to a Kähler omega_*, using either K_{omega_epsilon} epsilon^m or K_{omega_*} epsilon^m. No degenerate auxiliary limit is claimed. A compensated base change beta'=beta+ddc h>0, phi'=phi-h, for smooth h preserves the operator and changes energy by E_{beta'}(phi-h)=E_beta(phi)-E_beta(h).

Published foundations used, with exact scopes. Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Acta Math.149 (1982), 1–40, Section 2, constructs closed positive products of locally bounded psh functions by the recursion ddc v wedge S=ddc(v S), and proves weak continuity of their mixed products along locally uniformly bounded decreasing psh sequences. Smooth closed factors may be inserted. Products depend only on the currents. This is recalled in BEGZ arXiv:0812.3674v2, Section 1.2, LF175–188, and its decreasing continuity is explicitly used at LF651–658. Only this bounded decreasing theorem is used. On smaller coordinate balls, smooth decreasing bounded psh approximants are supplied by radial convolution: spherical subharmonic means increase with radius, so shrinking radii give decreasing approximations. Composition with a holomorphic map preserves their psh property and bounded decreasing limit.

Bounded symmetry and multilinearity follow by approximating finitely many local potentials smoothly and decreasingly, using smooth symmetry/multilinearity and passing to this theorem; sums of approximants still decrease and are locally uniformly bounded. Thus the explicitly omitted proof of general nonpluripolar multilinearity in BEGZ Proposition 1.4 is not a premise. Signed differences follow by linearity. Smooth closed backgrounds have local smooth ddc-potentials, so every actual factor here has a bounded psh local potential.

BEGZ Theorem 1.14 states: if A is closed complete pluripolar, Theta is closed positive of bidimension (1,1), varphi_i and psi_i are quasi-psh and locally bounded off A, and a=varphi_1-varphi_2 and b=psi_1-psi_2 are globally bounded, then the finite integrals satisfy

int_{Y\A} a ddc b Theta = int_{Y\A} b ddc a Theta = -int_{Y\A} db wedge dc a wedge Theta.

Its Lemma 1.15 gives finite Dirichlet mass for bounded differences on the stated bounded locus. In all uses here A is empty, Y compact Kähler, Theta a positive closed mixed BT product of d-1 factors, and the functions are smooth or differences of globally bounded quasi-psh functions. All hypotheses therefore hold. The bounded Dirichlet measure da wedge dc a wedge Theta is positive: locally it is defined by polarization from ddc v^2=2v ddc v+2dv wedge dc v for bounded nonnegative psh v, with positivity preserved under the decreasing approximation in the theorem's proof. Normalization changes only multiply these identities by a positive constant. The exact primary theorem and lemma bodies are retained at BEGZ LF626–762.

BEGZ Definition 1.17 and its following discussion, LF810–840, define positive products of pseudoeffective classes by Kähler perturbation and state that for nef classes they equal cup products. Hence a nef class has volume its top self-intersection. Here numerical dimension means the nef convention max{k:int_X theta^k kappa^{n-k}>0} for a Kähler kappa, equivalently the greatest nonzero positive-product degree. No comparison with other definitions is assumed. BEGZ is Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi, Monge–Ampère equations in big cohomology classes, Acta Math.205 (2010),199–262; the retained primary version is arXiv:0812.3674v2. The catalogue, proposal, comparison papers, and previous verdicts are not premises. We also use distributional Stokes and Sard's theorem that critical values of a smooth map have measure zero (A. Sard, Bull.Amer.Math.Soc.48 (1942),883–890); pi is smooth, so Sard applies.

Proof of the transverse constant and class claims. Properness follows from compactness. pi_*(omega^m) is a positive degree-zero current acting on top-degree test forms eta by int_X omega^m pi*eta. It is closed by Stokes and commutation of d with proper pushforward. A distribution with all first derivatives zero is constant on a connected manifold: locally convolve, obtaining smooth functions with zero derivative, hence constants; their distributional limit is constant, and constants agree on overlaps. This proves pi_*(omega^m)=c_omega>=0 globally, with no separate contribution supported on critical values.

Sard and surjectivity supply a regular value. The critical locus is closed in compact X, so its image is closed; its complement is open dense by Sard. On the inverse image of a neighbourhood of a regular value the map is a proper submersion. Submersion coordinates, a partition of unity and Fubini identify the pushforward there with fibre integration. Thus c_omega=int_{X_b}omega^m>0 for every regular value b; all connected components of this nonempty compact smooth m-dimensional fibre are included. This describes generic fibres, not a volume definition on exceptional fibres. Globally,

c_omega V_B=int_X theta^nu omega^m.

The right side is cohomological by Stokes, proving representative independence and showing c_{omega_epsilon}->c_{omega_*}>0 under smooth convergence. Since theta>=0 and theta+t kappa>0, alpha=[theta] is nef and pseudoeffective. theta^{nu+1}=0 pointwise; theta has rank nu on the regular locus, so int_X theta^nu kappa^m>0 for every Kähler kappa. Thus its numerical dimension is nu and, by the cited nef-volume statement, its volume is zero. Directly,

M_epsilon=int_X(theta+epsilon omega)^n
=sum_{k=0}^nu binom(n,k)epsilon^{n-k}int_X theta^k omega^{n-k}
=K_omega V_B epsilon^m+O(epsilon^{m+1}).

Bounded mass and exact-current lemma. If T_i=eta_i+ddc v_i are positive currents with bounded global potentials and positive/semipositive smooth closed backgrounds, and S is the product of the other d-1 positive factors, local BT recursion gives ddc v_i wedge S=ddc(v_i S). Indeed subtract the recursion for the bounded psh local potential of T_i and the smooth local potential of eta_i; smooth multiplication obeys the ordinary closed-current rule. These expressions glue, and v_i S has measure coefficients multiplied by a bounded Borel function. Its ddc integrates to zero on compact Y by testing against 1. Replacing factors one at a time, always with positive/semipositive backgrounds in this application, gives

int_Y T_1...T_d=int_Y eta_1...eta_d.

For any bounded difference w of potentials with the same background, the same recursion gives ddc w S=ddc(w S). Therefore for every smooth g,

int_Y g ddc w S=int_Y w ddc g S.

All measures here are finite by the mass identity. These statements use no unbounded mass comparison. For two nonsmooth bounded weights use the precisely checked BEGZ integration-by-parts theorem above.

Projection through singular fibres. Put H=theta+ddc U. For 0<=a<=nu we claim

pi_*(H^a theta^{nu-a}omega^m)=c_omega C^a beta^{nu-a}.

On a base coordinate ball write beta=ddc rho. The locally bounded psh q=rho+phi has smooth decreasing locally uniformly bounded psh approximants q_j on a smaller ball. On the ENTIRE inverse image, q_j composed with pi are smooth psh, decreasing locally uniformly boundedly to q composed with pi. BT continuity gives convergence of their mixed products to H^a theta^{nu-a}omega^m. For tests compactly supported in the smaller base ball, pullback supports are compact by properness, so a finite chart cover on X permits pushforward of this local convergence. At every smooth approximation the projection formula, directly from the definition of pushforward, gives

pi_*((pi*ddc q_j)^a theta^{nu-a}omega^m)=c_omega(ddc q_j)^a beta^{nu-a}.

The base decreasing BT theorem passes the right side to its limit. This proves the claim on every chart and hence globally, without removing critical values. Likewise smooth local approximants of any finite collection of bounded base potentials show that every product of more than nu horizontal factors vanishes: the smooth wedge vanishes already on the nu-dimensional base, and its BT limit is zero.

The displayed projection identity is an equality of positive top-degree Borel measures. The definition of measure pushforward consequently gives, for every bounded Borel g on B,

int_X(g composed with pi)H^a theta^{nu-a}omega^m=c_omega int_B g C^a beta^{nu-a}.

In particular g=phi is permitted even when discontinuous. This does not multiply a weakly convergent measure by a discontinuous function. The bounded mass lemma on B gives int_B C^a beta^{nu-a}=V_B. Bounded potentials have minimal singularities because every compact quasi-psh function is bounded above; against the positive background's reference 0, minimality conversely supplies a lower bound. This identifies the retained bounded/minimal type only.

Operator estimate. Set gamma=theta+epsilon omega, A=gamma+ddc u_epsilon, D=gamma+ddc U=H+epsilon omega, and w=u_epsilon-U. Bounded multilinearity and the exact-current lemma give

A^n-D^n=ddc w sum_{j=0}^{n-1}A^jD^{n-1-j}.

For a smooth real f on B choose C_f with -C_f beta<=ddc f<=C_f beta. Pullback preserves this inequality at critical points too. Each S_j=A^jD^{n-1-j} is positive closed, so the signed measure pi*ddc f S_j is dominated by C_f theta S_j. Smooth-test integration by parts and the mass lemma yield

|int_X(f composed with pi)(A^n-D^n)|<=n C_f delta_epsilon Q_epsilon,
Q_epsilon=int_X theta(theta+epsilon omega)^{n-1}
=sum_{k=0}^{nu-1}binom(n-1,k)epsilon^{n-1-k}int_X theta^{k+1}omega^{n-1-k}
=O(epsilon^m).

The first possible exponent is n-1-(nu-1)=m. Therefore the scaled error is O_f(delta_epsilon), with no relative rate. For the exact pullback family the projection/vanishing lemmas give

pi_*D^n/(K_omega epsilon^m)=C^nu+R_epsilon,
R_epsilon=sum_{k=0}^{nu-1}[binom(n,k)/K_omega]epsilon^{nu-k}pi_*(H^k omega^{n-k}).

This is a positive measure of mass

||R_epsilon||_TV=sum_{k=0}^{nu-1}[binom(n,k)/K_omega]epsilon^{nu-k}int_X theta^k omega^{n-k}=O(epsilon).

No smoothness of those lower-order pushforwards is assumed. The full bound for a smooth f is

|<pi_*A^n/(K_omega epsilon^m)-C^nu,f>|
<=[n C_f Q_epsilon/(K_omega epsilon^m)]delta_epsilon+||f||_infinity||R_epsilon||_TV.

Scaled positive masses equal M_epsilon/(K_omega epsilon^m)->V_B by the mass lemma. Smooth functions uniformly approximate continuous functions on compact B; this uniform mass bound controls the test approximation error. Thus the convergence holds for every continuous test, proving the operator assertion and its raw mass. Dividing instead by M_epsilon, which is positive only at positive epsilon, yields the probability limit C^nu/V_B. That convention does not reconstruct V_B from I-equivalence, and no zero mass is normalized here.

Full bounded energy calculus. On a d-dimensional compact Kähler Y with Kähler gamma let u,v be bounded gamma-psh, w=u-v, u_t=v+tw, T_t=(1-t)T_v+tT_u. By bounded multilinearity, e(t)=E_gamma(u_t) is a finite polynomial, so it can be differentiated without a global smoothing argument. With Theta=T_t^{j-1}gamma^{d-j}, the published bounded integration theorem applies: A is empty and both weights are bounded quasi-psh differences. It gives

(d+1)e'(t)=sum_{j=0}^d int w T_t^j gamma^{d-j}
+sum_{j=1}^d j int u_t ddc w T_t^{j-1}gamma^{d-j}
=sum_{j=0}^d int w T_t^j gamma^{d-j}
+sum_{j=1}^d j int w(T_t-gamma)T_t^{j-1}gamma^{d-j}
=(d+1)int w T_t^d.

Intermediate coefficients cancel as 1+j-(j+1)=0. Integrating in t and using int_0^1 binom(d,a)t^a(1-t)^{d-a}dt=1/(d+1) gives

E_gamma(u)-E_gamma(v)=1/(d+1)sum_{a=0}^d int (u-v)T_u^aT_v^{d-a}.

This is the cocycle because it is a difference of one functional. The derivative int w T_t^d is nonnegative when w>=0, proving monotonicity. Every mixed mass is M_gamma=int gamma^d, so E_gamma(0)=0 and E_gamma(u+b)=E_gamma(u)+bM_gamma. Thus monotonicity gives |E_gamma(u)-E_gamma(v)|<=M_gamma||u-v||_infinity. A second polynomial differentiation and the checked integration theorem with a=b=w, Theta=T_t^{d-1}, give

e''(t)=d int w ddc w T_t^{d-1}=-d int dw wedge dc w wedge T_t^{d-1}<=0.

The Dirichlet integral is finite by the cited bounded theorem/lemma and positive as described above; hence the energy is concave. The variational identity holds for all affine bounded psh segments, and by the identical polynomial calculation for differentiable paths in a finite-dimensional affine span of fixed bounded potentials that stay psh. It is not asserted for arbitrary infinite-dimensional or unbounded paths.

Energy limit. The supnorm estimate gives

|E_gamma(u_epsilon)-E_gamma(U)|/(K_omega epsilon^m)<=delta_epsilon M_epsilon/(K_omega epsilon^m)->0.

Expand E_gamma(U)=1/(n+1)sum_{j=0}^n int_X U(H+epsilon omega)^j(theta+epsilon omega)^{n-j}. Products with more than nu horizontal factors vanish. The coefficient of epsilon^m is

1/(n+1)sum_{a=0}^nu[sum_{j=0}^n binom(j,a)binom(n-j,nu-a)]int_X U H^a theta^{nu-a}omega^m.

The bracket is binom(n+1,nu+1): count (nu+1)-element subsets of {1,...,n+1} by their (a+1)-st member j+1, choosing a earlier and nu-a later members. Out-of-range binomials are zero. Dividing by n+1 gives binom(n,nu)/(nu+1), and the Borel-weight projection identity with g=phi makes this coefficient K_omega E_beta(phi). Every remaining term has k<nu horizontal factors and exponent n-k>=m+1. Its weighted integral is bounded by ||phi||_infinity int_X theta^k omega^{n-k}, by positivity and the mass lemma. Finitely many terms therefore give

E_gamma(U)=K_omega epsilon^m E_beta(phi)+O(epsilon^{m+1}).

Together these facts prove the energy limit. The base variational identity is d/dt E_beta(phi_t)=int_B dot(phi_t)C_{phi_t}^nu in the stated segment/finite-dimensional scope; hence the operator is the derivative of the limiting energy with no remaining auxiliary factor. This is structural support for P15.2, not a separate solution claim for P15.1.

Independence and reference changes. All arguments above hold for every fixed auxiliary Kähler class with its corresponding positive c_omega, giving the identical base limits. For omega_epsilon->omega_*>0 smoothly, c_{omega_epsilon}->c_{omega_*}>0 and every finite cohomological coefficient in the mass, mixed estimate, positive remainder and energy expansion converges and is bounded. Repeat the exact formulas at each epsilon: all error estimates are uniform, so the same conclusions follow without a rate or epsilon derivatives. The ratio of the two allowed calibrations tends to 1.

For beta'=beta+ddc h>0, put H_h=h composed with pi, gamma'=pi*beta'+epsilon omega, phi'=phi-h and u'_epsilon=u_epsilon-H_h. Then beta'+ddc phi'=C and gamma'+ddc u'_epsilon=gamma+ddc u_epsilon exactly; the supnorm error and transverse constant are unchanged, and int_B(beta')^nu=V_B by Stokes. The operator is therefore unchanged. The bounded relative-energy formula applied to phi,h proves

E_beta(phi)-E_beta(h)=1/(nu+1)sum_{a=0}^nu int_B(phi-h)C^a(beta')^{nu-a}=E_{beta'}(phi-h).

On X it likewise gives E_{gamma'}(u_epsilon-H_h)=E_gamma(u_epsilon)-E_gamma(H_h); H_h is gamma-psh since gamma+ddc H_h=pi*beta'+epsilon omega>0, and its scaled limit supplies the same reference correction. This does not assert invariance under changing the base class or the supplied fibration.

Residual scope. The proof covers the full supplied smooth-manifold fibration scope with bounded base potentials, singular/dimension-jumping fibres, non-descending bounded approximating potentials, arbitrary fixed auxiliary Kähler classes after calibration, and smoothly convergent nondegenerate auxiliary paths. It does not construct a fibration or canonical carrier for general pseudoeffective zero-volume classes, prove minimality of reference choices, extend to unbounded prescribed P-types/E1, or address degenerate auxiliary limits or nonuniform potential convergence. No optional continuous-descent theorem is a premise or a new claim. The original P15.2 remains open: status partial, candidate false.

Artifacts and rerun. All new mathematics, imported theorem statements, applicability checks, and the complete proof with verbatim primary appendix are in P15.2-argument.md. The standalone full-proof paper is P15.2-partial.tex and its twice-compiled PDF is P15.2-partial.pdf. Run python rerun.py for exact finite diagnostics and the two-pass build; run python prepare_evidence.py for source-copy/LF reproduction. status.json has exactly id,status,exact_result,proof_file,concrete_gaps. author-audit.md and research-log.md record the self-audit and research. Source/build/environment/original-input evidence is retained locally. Execution success does not verify the analytic proof.

notes.text:
This note records observations and exhaustive finite diagnostic results for the author theorem draft in n1; it is not a mathematical proof by execution.

The exact arithmetic program checked n=2,...,32, nu=1,...,n-1, a=0,...,nu. All 5,952 instances of sum_{j=0}^n binom(j,a)binom(n-j,nu-a)=binom(n+1,nu+1), together with division by n+1, passed. For each of 496 (n,nu) pairs it checked min_{k<=nu}(n-k)=m, min_{k<=nu-1}(n-1-k)=m, and min_{k<nu}(n-k)=m+1. It also checked the telescoping coefficient vector [0,...,0,d+1] and exact beta-integral coefficients 1/(d+1) for d=1,...,32. These finite checks do not prove the formulas for arbitrary dimensions; n1 supplies their general derivations.

Fourteen recorded copied-source hashes were rechecked, as were all three original decoded input strings. The full source text SHA256 is 9d52c95247fd7f69194c84df01ef54b4cd98b6e4e35b4f3851f90f04c98a71b0; the primary PDF SHA256 is 43097be8459edfd948929fade34367fa7bbd0fe691d9cba1a4f27a11181214cd. The proposal SHA256 is 10adbd0671ec244edf80ed819c540ae1e8df14d60c9efea66ddd8383dfa6789b. All six supplied unit hashes match the inclusive LF175–188, 189–242, 249–322, 626–762, 810–840, and 1120–1222 slices, split only on LF and joined without a terminal LF. Their full bodies, including printed defects and omitted proof language, appear verbatim in the authoritative Markdown appendix. No earlier comparison-paper theorem or verdict is a premise.

The standalone full-proof PDF has 10 pages. Both retained pdflatex passes returned exit code zero with no warnings, overfull boxes, or underfull boxes. Four required PDF text-presence checks passed after whitespace normalization. The first build had a misplaced tag for formula (19) inside an aligned environment; moving the tag outside changed no formula. Initial failed TeX, command record, and output are retained. A subsequent successful two-pass build was followed by a substring check that failed because a phrase wrapped across a PDF line; the check now normalizes whitespace. These are document/diagnostic issues, not rejected analytic proof steps.

The author self-audit checked the closed degree-zero pushforward, full-inverse-image bounded projection, Borel-weight identity, cohomological mixed masses, empty-exceptional-set BEGZ integration-by-parts applicability, the epsilon exponent in the non-descending perturbation estimate, bounded energy coefficient, class-dependent calibration, and reference cocycle. It found no unresolved indispensable step within the supplied-fibration bounded scope. This is a self-audit only; original P15.2 remains open.

Programs and artifacts: run python rerun.py to repeat the arithmetic diagnostics and two-pass build. The compilation command is pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error -file-line-error P15.2-partial.tex, executed twice. Run python prepare_evidence.py to recreate/check source copies and LF slices. Command arrays and statuses are in evidence/commands.json, results in evidence/diagnostics.json, stdout/stderr in evidence/rerun.stdout.txt and evidence/rerun.stderr.txt, pass logs in evidence/build-pass-1.log and evidence/build-pass-2.log, PDF extraction in evidence/P15.2-partial-extracted.txt, provenance in evidence/source-provenance.json, environment details in evidence/environment.json, and preserved failures in evidence/initial-failed-*. Original decoded strings and byte input are in original-input/. The complete proof and source applicability checks are P15.2-argument.md; paper/PDF are P15.2-partial.tex and P15.2-partial.pdf; the author audit and research log are author-audit.md and research-log.md. status.json has the required five keys; notes.json retains the canonical notes.

Observed tools were Python 3.12.14, pandoc 3.1.11.1, and pdfTeX 3.141592653-2.6-1.40.26 (TeX Live 2025/dev/Debian), on Linux x86_64. Copied operator configuration specifies Xean native Codex gpt-6.1-sol at xhigh. No extra provider/model, subagent, network, installation, external message, authentication/runtime changes, or resource-heavy computation was used.
